logline: A young Derg-era sailor breaks his arm two days before his ship sails for Massawa; the ship never returns, and the fall he cursed becomes the reason he preaches.
audience: My family, especially cousins and siblings in Addis Ababa and abroad who know only fragments of my uncle's story, and Amharic-speaking followers. They watch on a phone, vertical, usually after it is forwarded on Telegram or TikTok.
intent: When it ends they should feel how close he came (two days, one slip) and gratitude rather than triumph, understand why he now says 'let God lead your life', and remember the comrades who did not come back.

style.block: hand-painted gouache illustration, visible brush strokes, soft paper grain, muted palette of Red Sea teal, rust red and warm ochre, gentle cinematic light, main subject centered in frame, late 1980s Ethiopia, no text, no lettering
style.negative: photorealistic, photograph, text, letters, watermark, logo, extra fingers, deformed hands, modern objects, gore, blood

uncle_now.description: the same Ethiopian man now in his late fifties, short grey hair, short grey beard, kind eyes, simple white shirt

commander.description: a kind Ethiopian ship captain in his forties with a moustache, dark navy jacket and simple sailor cap, gentle fatherly posture, mostly in soft backlight

voice.style_instruction: Say slowly and warmly, like a nephew telling his family an old story:

music.caption: instrumental, slow Ethiopian tizita ballad, solo krar and soft masenqo over a low drone, sparse, intimate, warm tape texture, no drums, no vocals

cues.purpose: Memory. Tizita is the mode of longing; it tells an Ethiopian ear this is a remembered story.
The dream of Massawa: the theme is stated warmly, once.
The fall: sparse and uneasy, the ground shifts.
Despair: almost nothing, a low drone.
The loss: the music stops; only the sea. Silence is the loudest cue.
Grace: the Massawa theme returns, transformed into a brighter mode.
